causal.assumptions_right: The bill, not the currency, was the right place to test the Australia path, and leaving once the strip stepped down kept the miss small.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: A contract already above cash was treated as a hike still to come. The chance that the strip would step down from the front was underweighted.
causal.causal_divergence: The pay needed a higher implied rate. The strip stepped down instead, so the hike-cycle thesis was not what the bills delivered.
causal.future_implication: The next Australian bill pay has to be a contract that is actually on a hike path. That is why the September Australia pay is closed today.
causal.observed_reality: The pay was closed on 13 November after the Australian strip stepped down and the contract was marked lower.
causal.original_belief: June 2027 Australia bills were only a modest step above cash, so an underpriced hiking cycle would lift the contract.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same strip, the June pay would have been closed once contracts were stepping down from the front, rather than held as a hawkish identity trade.

facts.invalidation: The view breaks if the US 10-year reverses away from the 2002 high together with a break in oil while Sep-27 SOFR and Jun-27 AONIA stop repricing higher, or if Jun-27 AONIA trades up through the AU 10-year at 5.245 and the cash-to-contract gap is closed.

items.future_rule: Keep an Australian bill pay only while that contract is on a hike path above cash. A strip that is flat in front and lower in the back is an exit.
items.lesson: An Australian bill pay is not an underpriced hiking cycle once the strip is flat at the front and lower in the back.
items.thesis_assessment: A contract already above the then cash rate was treated as a hike that still had to be priced. The later strip was flat to lower.
items.what_failed: The June 2027 Australia pay failed as an underpriced hiking cycle. The strip stepped down instead of extending.

causal.assumptions_right: The bill was the right instrument, and the next-day exit recognized that the back of the strip was ease rather than a fresh hike.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Opening a contract already below cash treated a hawkish bias as a reason to pay a cut the strip was still pricing.
causal.causal_divergence: The intended mark was a rise toward the cash anchor. One session later the contract had not risen and the position was closed.
causal.future_implication: Do not keep a short that is the easy side of cash. The same exit rule closes the remaining September Australia pay.
causal.observed_reality: The pay was closed one day later with the strip still pricing a contract under cash near 4.85.
causal.original_belief: December 2027 Australia bills under the cash rate would be taken out, so the priced ease was a pay.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same strip the December pay would not have been opened. If it had been opened, the next-day cover would still have been the action.

facts.invalidation: The new pay is wrong if December 2027 AONIA falls further below 4.65 while the front of the Australian strip drops back and the US December step is marked back toward an unchanged path.

items.no_new_lesson: The small loss one day after entry is bounded variance inside the risk budget. The original process remains sound because the pay was closed the next session once the strip still priced ease rather than a hike.
items.thesis_assessment: The ease-fade was not confirmed. Closing it the next session kept the miss small instead of turning a below-cash pay into a campaign.
items.what_failed: The December 2027 Australia pay was opened on the easy side of cash and did not rise toward the cash anchor in the one session it was held.
